summary: Mozambique's official eVisa portal sorts visitors into four groups: 17 nationalities, mostly from southern and eastern Africa, are visa-exempt for 30 or 90 days; 29 others, including the US, the UK, Canada, Japan and much of Western Europe, need an Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA) for stays of up to 30 days; citizens of Pakistan, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Nepal and Somalia must apply at an embassy; and everyone else applies online for an eVisa before travel.

tips.text: Australia's Smartraveller says do not travel to Cabo Delgado province, the Erati and Memba districts of Nampula province, or the Marrupa and Mecula districts of Niassa province, because of the threat of terrorism and kidnapping.
The UK government says you must have your passport with you at all times, and that police patrols and checkpoints are common and will not accept copies or photos of it.
Canada's travel advice says visa fees can be paid on arrival by credit card or in accepted currencies; no official source we could read publishes the eVisa fee.
The UK government says cyclones and floods are common in the rainy season from November to April, often causing landslides, road closures and disruption to transport.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Mozambique?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. Mozambique's official eVisa portal (evisa.gov.mz) lists 17 nationalities, mostly from southern and eastern Africa, as visa-exempt for 30 or 90 days. Citizens of 29 countries, including the US, the UK, Canada, Portugal and most of Western Europe, need an Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA) before travel, for stays of up to 30 days. Citizens of Pakistan, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Nepal and Somalia cannot use the portal and must apply at a Mozambican embassy. Everyone else applies online for an eVisa before travelling.

faq.question: Is there a fee for the eTA?
faq.answer: Decree 10/2023, which exempted citizens of 29 countries from the visa, sets a MZN 650 processing fee, payable when pre-registering at evisa.gov.mz at least 48 hours before boarding; the portal now lists these countries under the eTA scheme. The UK Foreign Office says British travellers also pay a USD 37 visa fee (about USD 47 in total), online. The portal itself does not publish the eTA fee.

faq.question: Can I get a Mozambique visa on arrival?
faq.answer: No official Mozambican source we could read says so today. The migration service's visa rules, which described a border visa, cannot be read: its site does not answer and the newest archived copy is from 2024. The official eVisa portal does not offer a visa on arrival: it sorts nationalities into visa-exempt, eTA, eVisa and embassy-only, and tells travellers to carry the printed approval for arrival.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Mozambique?
faq.answer: It depends on how you entered. Canada's travel advice says you may request one 30-day extension from the immigration authorities, that justification may be required and fees may apply, and that overstaying without authorisation may result in fines. For an eVisa, Mozambique's official eVisa portal says that if you need to extend your stay you must contact the Mozambique Embassy directly.

faq.question: Is Mozambique safe for tourists?
faq.answer: Australia's Smartraveller advises a high degree of caution in Mozambique overall and says do not travel to Cabo Delgado province and parts of Nampula and Niassa provinces, nor on stretches of the EN1 and EN6 roads. The UK government says you must carry your passport at all times.
